nodes.summary: A group $G$ is simply reducible when the character of every irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$ is real-valued, and for all irreducible finite-dimensional complex representations $U$, $V$ and $W$ of $G$, the space $\mathrm{Hom}_G(U, V \otimes W)$ of $G$-equivariant linear maps from $U$ to the tensor product $V \otimes W$ has complex dimension at most $1$.
nodes.title: Simply reducible group

nodes.summary: Every finite simply reducible group is soluble; that is, the statement of Kourovka Problem 11.94 holds.
nodes.title: Finite simply reducible groups are soluble

nodes.summary: The statement, asked by S. P. Strunkov as Kourovka Problem 11.94, that every finite simply reducible group is soluble.
nodes.title: Solubility of finite simply reducible groups (Kourovka 11.94)
